biblical_reference.note: In the Hebrew Bible, Alon is used as a place name and as a personal name. For example, in Judges 9:11, Gideon's son Abimelech is described as ruling from Beit-El, which is also called Alon. In Isaiah 4:6, God is described as sitting above the cherubim and seraphim, surrounded by 'the foundations of the mountains and the fruitful trees of Alon'.
